newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia may ease tax burden on insurance policies.
newsitem.headline: Russia may ease tax burden on insurance policies.

text.p: Russia may consider easing the tax burden on life and pension insurance policies and issuing special state securities to help insurance firms stay solvent, a senior industry official said on Tuesday.

Konstantin Pylov, deputy chairman of the Commission for Supervision of Insurance Companies (Rosstrakhnadzor), told a news conference that the organisation had forwarded such proposals to the government.

"Our commission has prepared proposals that the Commission on Taxation Improvement include life insurance for over five years and pension insurance into production costs, and that it cut the tax brackets for individuals' life and pension insurance payments," he said.
He said the proposed measures could raise the volume of premiums on these types of insurance by seven trillion roubles from last year's 10.1 trillion roubles within a year or two.
"There must a mechanism to guarantee that insurance companies will be able to place these premiums," he added.
He also said Rosstrakhnadzor had proposed that the government issue five-year to 10-year paper for insurance firms.

Russia's insurance market is dominated by risk insurance which does not bring high profits and deprives insurance companies from becoming serious investors able to manage their portfolios and obligations.
Russian insurances paid out 9.7 trillion roubles on volunitary policies out of 10.1 trillion roubles collected for this purpose in 1996, Pylov said.
Russia's total 1996 insurance premiums were about 27.4 trillion roubles.
